title: Java serialization
context: What is Java serialization, and why is it risky?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Serialization turns an object graph into bytes, so it can be stored or sent, and deserialization rebuilds it. A class opts in by implementing `Serializable`. Its risks are large. Deserializing untrusted data can run gadget chains that execute code. Class changes break old data unless you set `serialVersionUID`. The format is bulky and slow. Prefer JSON or a schema-based format with explicit DTOs. If you must use Java serialization, add an allow-list filter for classes.

points.title: Untrusted input
points.why: Deserializing attacker-controlled bytes can execute code through gadget classes.

points.title: Versioning
points.why: Set serialVersionUID so a compatible class change does not break old data.
